subject: remote workers
one_liner: Verified-fan ticketing for the meetings you were already invited to.
brand_voice_notes: Box-office confidence applied to calendar invites. Standby talks about stand-ups like stadium dates: presales, tours, sections, sold-out notices. Fees are never apologised for, only itemised. The product believes remote employees have been attending meetings for free for too long and that this is a market inefficiency.

hero.h1: Your all-hands is sold out. You are in the queue.
hero.sub: Standby brings dynamic pricing, presale codes and a service fee to every video call your company runs. Remote staff can finally buy the meetings they used to attend for free.

features.title: Dynamic tile pricing
features.blurb: Camera-on seats next to the CEO's tile reprice every 4 seconds based on demand. At last quarter's kickoff, a front-row tile resold for $1,140 to a man in accounts payable.

features.title: Verified Colleague presale
features.blurb: Prove you are a real employee and not a bot by attending 3 optional socials. Presale codes go to the email address you were offboarded from in 2022.

features.title: All-in pricing, eventually
features.blurb: Every seat shows a clear base price. The Facilitation Fee, the Unmute Fee and the Home Wi-Fi Convenience Charge appear at checkout, where they belong.

demo_screen_concept: A box-office seat map for 'Q4 All-Hands: The Alignment Tour 2026'. The video-call grid is drawn as a venue: the CEO's tile is the stage, and 36 participant tiles below are seats split into sections (Front Grid, Mid Grid, Obstructed View behind the screen-share, and Audio-Only Standing). Each tile shows a live price that drifts every few seconds. A sticky queue banner counts your position down from #48,211. Click tiles to select seats, filter by section or 'camera-on required', and open a checkout drawer where fees (Facilitation, Unmute, Home Wi-Fi Convenience, Order Processing For This Order) stack up under a small base price, with a 'price changed while you were deciding' toast.

design_direction.style: Retro box-office ticket stock, matinee daylight mode. An event-ticketing SaaS printed like a 1970s theatre ticket and box-office window: cream ticket card stock, rose-red ink, flat fills with no gradients, rounded retro display type, and monospace seat codes. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: race bibs, split clocks, pace lines, motion slants, trail signs, blazes, contour lines, label tape, crossed-out names, middle slots, fridge magnets, ghost text, keycaps, squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration, activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands, aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, barcodes. Also absent: dark page backgrounds, serif type, glassmorphism, blur, drop shadows other than flat 0 3px 0, condensed signage type. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The ticket stub: features, tiers and testimonials are cream tickets with a dashed perforation, half-circle punched notches on both edges at the perforation, and a narrow stub carrying an ADMIT ONE vertical label. (2) The seat code: every section header reads like a seat assignment in mono ('SEC 02 · ROW F · SEAT 14'). (3) The fee stack: every price is followed by a smaller itemised fee list that is always longer than the price. (4) The queue strip: a sticky rose strip at the top counting down 'You are #48,211 in line' with a progress bar that never passes 3%.

palette.name: Ticket Stock and Box Office Rose

design_direction.archetype: Event marketplace landing: queue-strip header, ticket-stub hero with the primary CTA as a 'get tickets' button, feature stubs, testimonial stubs as 'reviews from the venue', pricing as a three-ticket fee-stacked tier row, closing 'final presale' CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Ticket tear: stubs slide 6px on hover along the perforation. Queue counter ticks down by small random amounts every 1.2s. Prices flicker to a new value with a 200ms colour flash. Respects prefers-reduced-motion by freezing counters.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left: big Righteous headline in ink with 'sold out' set in rose; sub and CTA beneath. Right: one oversized admission ticket rotated -3deg showing the event 'Q4 All-Hands: The Alignment Tour 2026', venue 'Zoom, Room 4', seat code and an itemised fee stack. The queue strip pins above everything.
